svg.text: cross opening at z = 0.30, above the lead-in chamfer
1. Dimensions in mm. First-angle projection (ISO 128). Scale as marked per view.
3. Geometry re-authored from keycap_stem.scad in build123d. The STEP is the shape reference;
THIS DRAWING governs tolerance, material and finish.
4. CRITICAL MX cross 4.05 x 1.10 ±0.03, R0.30 corner fillets. Gauge against a reference MX
switch stem, not by CMM alone. Polish the core pin to draw along the arms.
5. CRITICAL The transparent relegendable cap is an off-the-shelf POS part, so that mating
dimension is a hard datum set by a supplier we do not control. Confirm before cutting steel.
6. Draft, measured off the model: outer body 11.6°, inside pocket 18.4°, centre pocket 33.0°.
7. ZERO DRAFT on the display seat (12.2 x 12.1 x 1.1 deep) and on its cable relief. Shallow enough
that it often releases as-is, but confirm it rather than discover it at first article.
8. Cross draft 0.08° on the flats and 0.31° at the arm tips, opening downward -- the core pin
withdraws in the correct direction, but with very little relief.
9. MATERIAL ABS, chosen for shrink: 0.4-0.7% is what keeps the MX cross inside note 4.
Dimensions are the FINISHED PART -- apply shrink to the cavity and state the rate used.
10. Stamp "S β" = profile + revision, 0.30 deep, zero draft, in the display-seat floor
and the pocket ceiling. Revision character is U+03B2 GREEK SMALL LETTER BETA --
the MOULDED part is deliberately β where the 3D-printed prototypes are α, so the two are
told apart by eye. Carry it on a REPLACEABLE INSERT in the cavity rather than cut into the
block: a revision change is then a plug swap, not a tool edit. Font: Noto Sans Bold.
11. Three 0.40 x 3.00 x 0.30 tabs stand 0.20 proud of the body (+Y and ±X). They are a print-plate
aid carried over from the 3D-printed part -- delete them for tooling unless you want them.
